`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Two structural signals in this shard are worth naming before the verdicts. First, kaikki's *umbrella headers* — a candidate ending in a colon like `"to infect:"` or `"to entrust in various ways:"` — are entry-structure metadata, not definitions; `anstecken` shortened past its umbrella correctly, `anvertrauen` shipped the umbrella itself. Second, several German verbs here are *causative/intransitive pairs* (`auferstehen`/`auferwecken`, `aufwecken`/`auferwecken`), and a vague English gloss on one member silently collapses the pair — which is exactly how the `niederführen`/`niederfahren` defect happened.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I've read all 50 verbs. Writing the findings now.

Wrote `verbdata/gloss-review/shards/gloss_004.out.json` — 5 findings across the 50 verbs in shard 4.

| Verb | Shipped | Severity | Replacement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anvertrauen` | entrust in various ways | low | entrust |
| `aufarbeiten` | refurbish | medium | work through |
| `aufatmen` | breathe again | medium | breathe a sigh of relief |
| `aufbleiben` | wake, stay awake, stay up | medium | stay up, stay awake |
| `auferwecken` | raise up, awaken | medium | resurrect, raise from the dead |

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Three of the five are *literalism* defects rather than wrong-sense picks: `aufatmen`, `aufbleiben`, and `auferwecken` all ship a gloss assembled from the parts (auf + atmen, auf + bleiben) instead of what the compound conventionally means. That's a distinct failure mode from the `fernschauen` pattern in the brief — there the right sense existed further down the list; here kaikki offered only the literal reading, so no import rule keyed on `sense_index` would surface them. `aufbleiben` adds a second twist: "wake" is correct English, but only in the archaic vigil-keeping sense, so the defect is in *English* register rather than German semantics.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Notable near-misses I deliberately did not flag: `anspringen` "jump at, pounce" (the engine-starting sense is common, but the shipped literal one is equally core), `anstehen` "stand in a queue" (competes with "be pending," both frequent), and `anstoßen` "push something" (loses the nudge/toast nuance but isn't wrong). Each is thin rather than misleading, which the brief puts below the bar.
